19 to 23 inches, light reddish brown (5YR 6/5) loam, yellowish red (5YR 4/5) moist; massive; hard, friable, slightly sticky, slightly plastic; many very fine roots; common very fine and few fine tubular pores; 30 percent flat burned shale fragments; moderately calcareous with lime crust on underside of shale fragments; moderately alkaline; abrupt wavy boundary.
C3 23 to 60 inches, fragmented hard red burned shale with roots matted between shale layers in upper 2 inches.
Depth to the platy shale and sandstone is 20 to 30 inches. Shale fragments in the A and B horizons range from 2 to 10 percent and in the C horizons from 10 to 35 percent. The clay content of the B2 and C1 horizons ranges from 20 to 30 percent. The A horizon color includes weak red and brown.
The B2 horizon color includes yellowish red, red, and light red. Soil color hue is 7.5YR to 10R.
Spearman soils are associated with Chugter and Wibaux soils. They have less depth to platy shale than the Chugter soils. They are deeper to hard platy shale and contain fewer coarse fragments than the Wibaux soil.
Spearman loam, undulating (4 to 8 percent slopes) (St).
This soil is in 10 to 30 acre areas on burned shale highlands. It occupies wide ridges between deep valleys and on the divides at the heads of two or more valleys. The soil profile is the one described as typical for the series. Included with this soil in mapping along the ridge tops are areas of Cushman loam, Thedalund loam, and Wibaux channery loam.
The surface runoff is medium, and the erosion hazard is moderate.
This soil is suited to dryland crops and range. The spots of Wibaux soils interfere with normal tillage operations.
(Capability Unit IIIe-3 Dryland; Silty range site 10-14 inch precipitation zone; Windbreak Suitability Group 2M)
Spearman-Wibaux complex, rolling (4 to 15 percent slopes) (SU).
This complex comprises rolling soils of the sedimentary plains. Slopes are mainly 8 to 15 percent but range downward to 4 percent. The complex consists of 40 to 60 percent Spearman loam, 30 to 50 percent Wibaux loam and stony loam and 5 to 20 percent Thedalund loam. The Spearman loam is in the swales between hills, on wide ridges and the heads of drainageways.
